newsitem.title: PANAMA: Panama destroys notoriously violent Modelo prison.
newsitem.headline: Panama destroys notoriously violent Modelo prison.

text.p: Panamanian authorities destroyed notoriously violent Modelo prison on Tuesday, ending what President Ernesto Perez Balladares called "a huge shame."
The president pushed a button that activated about 200 pounds (90 kg) of dynamite to bring down the jail, where guards had been filmed beating naked convicts.

"The world celebrates International Human Rights Day today ... Panama couldn't unite in such a celebration before," Perez Balladares told an official ceremony. "Never will something like this happen again ... We have ended a huge shame."
The blast was set to bring down only half of the prison, since it sits in the middle of a residential community. The rest will be destroyed by cranes and bulldozers.

Built in 1925 for 275 prisoners, it has held up to 3,000 inmates and was described by a Roman Catholic bishop as "a small-scale hell." It became a centre of controversy in July when local television showed guards herding naked prisoners into an outdoor courtyard and beating them.
The guards were quelling a riot in which two prisoners were killed and nearly a dozen prisoners and guards wounded.
